_comment: THE SHIPPED LOOK: what the app opens on, and what a render uses when nobody picks a
preset. Every stage reads this file; nothing hardcodes a look value. The app renders
through its own copies, passed as LOOK_FILE, so it never edits this one — change the
shipped look by hand, it is just numbers.
convert.cube is THE RENDERING, and it is this app's own (luts/rendering/neutral.cube,
baked by scripts/make-rendering-lut.py). It takes the log picture to a finished one in a
single scene-referred step, so no stage downstream works on highlights that Apple's cube
has already squeezed into the top tenth of the range. Its contrast, saturation and black
are baked into the cube's TITLE rather than kept here: it is a shipped asset like the film
cubes, re-baked when it is re-tuned.
correct.* is the input-correction stage, which runs BEFORE the conversion and therefore in
log: exposure and white balance in linear (decoded and re-encoded with Apple's published
transfer function), then contrast and saturation in log. It is what a clip's Adjust and
metering add to. At the values below it does NOTHING, and a neutral correction leaves the
filter out of the graph rather than rendering every pixel through a lookup that returns it.
match.reference_stops is where a clip's metered log-average lands, in stops from mid grey;
scripts/solve-exposure.py meters each clip against it, in linear, before the conversion. It
is what makes a shoot land together.
halation is 0 here: a glow is a film effect, and the presets that want one carry it.
finish.* is the delivery stage: the log denoise, the edge-limited sharpener and the film
gauge. Like grain, none of it is in a still.
